items.what: Ufunc support for a dtype= keyword (np.positive(df, dtype=np.float32) must return a DataFrame with float32 dtypes); the instruction only mentions the out parameter
items.quote:
result = np.positive(df, dtype=np.float32)
    assert all(d == np.float32 for d in result.dtypes)

items.what: np.negative with out= must write into an int64 ndarray (sibling unary ufunc; same __array_ufunc__ out-handling fix covers it)
np.exp with out= writes to ndarray (sibling unary ufunc, same fix)

reason: The instruction only describes the out= bug; the dtype= keyword behavior for ufuncs (float32 dtypes) is an extra semantic the instruction never mentions, so it is not inferable. The other ufunc/out cases (negative, exp) are covered by the same minimal __array_ufunc__ out fix.
